Domainpad objects

Source: R/zz-gen-shared.R
go_domainpad.Rd

Sets the space in pixels to reserve inside the edges of `domain`. Because `domain` is a fraction of the plot area, the gap between subplots changes with the figure size. `domainpad` keeps the same size in pixels at all figure sizes, so it can hold content with a fixed size, such as a subplot title. x axes use `left` and `right`. y axes use `top` and `bottom`. If the padding needs more room than the domain has, the two pads shrink by the same factor, and the plot area keeps a length of at least 2 pixels. An axis that sets `overlaying` ignores its own `domainpad` and uses the `domainpad` of the axis it overlays, so that both axes share the same plot area. Used for domainpad in 2 places in the schema. go_domainpad() creates one; a named list with the same properties works too.

Usage

go_domainpad(
  arg = NULL,
  ...,
  bottom = NULL,
  left = NULL,
  right = NULL,
  top = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

Arguments

arg

Optional named list, or graph object of the same type, to initialise properties from. Named arguments take precedence.

...

Not used: properties must be named in full.

bottom

Sets the space in pixels to reserve inside the bottom edge of `domain`. Applies to y axes only. Number in the interval [0, Inf].

left

Sets the space in pixels to reserve inside the left edge of `domain`. Applies to x axes only. Number in the interval [0, Inf].

right

Sets the space in pixels to reserve inside the right edge of `domain`. Applies to x axes only. Number in the interval [0, Inf].

top

Sets the space in pixels to reserve inside the top edge of `domain`. Applies to y axes only. Number in the interval [0, Inf].

skip_invalid

If TRUE, silently drop invalid properties instead of raising an error.

Value

A go_domainpad object (a named list).

Details

These objects appear in 2 places in the plotly.js schema (properties named domainpad), all with the same properties and rules.

Examples

mtcars |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(x = ~wt, y = ~mpg, mode = "markers") |>
  update_layout(xaxis = go_xaxis(domainpad = go_domainpad()))
